title: Learned process groups expose different time profiles in traffic-fine records
summary: NMF-based process grouping in150370 traffic-fine records produced groups concentrated in different periods despite calendar dates being excluded from their encodings. Three groups had88-94% of traces ending in2000-2004, while two others had86-97% ending in2009-2013. These exploratory temporal associations do not identify the causes of process change.
organization: Fraunhofer IAIS; City St George’s, University of London; University of Seville; Eindhoven University of Technology; University of St. Gallen

source_review.scope: Primary v1 front and safe computational/model Methods, specific application Results and statistical limitations

evidence.tested: An analyst iteratively fitted NMF topics and formed process groups, with k-means used on topic weights in a later round. Posthoc end-date distributions compared accepted group memberships.
evidence.unknown: Group thresholds, encoding choices and commit order were analyst-selected on the same log. No reseed stability study or dedicated drift analysis separated behavior from calendar policy changes; late open cases can reflect right-censoring. The result is a data-specific association, not evidence of an administrative cause or improved process performance.
evidence.ai_role: Fitted topic representations and learned partitions supply behavior-based groups whose subsequently examined date distributions reveal the temporal contrast. UMAP is a visual aid rather than the enabling operation.
